account:
Today I have kept my morning office appointment, attended the scheduled ten o'clock mill inspection, returned home for lunch, and attended the thirteen o'clock office appointment. I am now at the neighbour's dockside cottage for fifteen o'clock tea. My next office appointment is sixteen-thirty.

The unusual matter is repeated, vague talk about a 'bridge or port change' at the bakery. Townsfolk 21 said the baker, freight, innkeeper and neighbour had been there, but gave no clear explanation of the change. Several other townsfolk repeated essentially the same phrase. That repetition is not independent confirmation of an actual change. The secretary heard an unintelligible distant shout from the baker this morning, but has received no reliable details or new council letters. I found nobody answering at the bakery when I visited. I have asked the secretary to seek a firsthand report from the baker and return for sixteen-thirty. I have just asked the neighbour whether they witnessed the discussion and what happened; I have not yet heard an answer. I cannot yet tell whether this concerns transport arrangements, a proposal, or something else, nor what its purpose is.

The mill inspection was also inconclusive. It had remained unconfirmed, and neither the secretary's earlier visits nor my inspection found responsible staff. The accessible mill stall contained seventy-six hay bales and 104 emeralds, but I found no delivery records. This is not a full grain-stock audit or evidence of wrongdoing. Townsfolk reported that the innkeeper carried hay from the mill; I did not see that myself and do not know its purpose. I asked the secretary to record the limitations of the inspection, identify the responsible mill contact, and arrange a confirmed follow-up. There may be ordinary business behind these events, but I currently lack the firsthand information needed to connect them.
